The age curve derivative is computed from a natural cubic spline fit to EPA contributions across player ages, capturing performance trends. Its derivative identifies peak performance ages (RB: 24.53, WR: 25.33, QB: 26.67). Pressure-to-sack rate models QB durability and scheme effectiveness, with declining rates indicating improved pocket protection. Each primitive exhibits distinct failure modes: CORE lacks early-season signal, age curves assume smooth performance evolution, and P/S rate assumes consistent data quality. These primitives form a dual framework for predictive modeling: CORE for team dynamics and age curves for individual trajectory, while P/S rate provides tactical insight into QB resilience.
